worksheet.title: Sort by Shape
worksheet.subtitle: Putting the same things together
worksheet.learning_goal: I can put the shapes that are the same together.

parts.title: Bit's shapes got mixed up
parts.text: Bit dropped a pile of shapes. Help Bit put the same shapes together. Making groups of the same thing is called SORTING.

parts.title: Bit's pile
parts.note: Look: circles, triangles, and squares are all mixed together.

parts.title: Watch Bit sort one group
parts.note: Bit put both circles ● in one group. Now you try the rest.

parts.title: Triangle group  ▲
parts.prompt: Draw all the triangles from the pile in this group.

parts.title: Square group  ■
parts.prompt: Draw all the squares from the pile in this group.

parts.title: You try
parts.prompt: Here is a new little pile: ■ ● ■. Draw only the squares in the boxes.

parts.title: Big idea
parts.text: Putting the same things together is called sorting. Computers sort too — it helps them find things fast!

parts.title: Goal
parts.text: Children sort a mixed set of shapes into groups by one attribute (shape). Sorting/classifying is a foundational computational-thinking skill — it is how computers organize information to find it quickly.

parts.title: Kindergarten frame (Ontario)
text: Problem Solving and Innovating — children use computational-thinking skills (sorting and classifying by attribute) to make sense of their world.
No reading is required of the child: read each prompt aloud; the child responds by drawing.

parts.title: Materials
parts.text: The printed worksheet + a pencil/crayon. Optional: real shape blocks or shape cut-outs to sort with hands first.

parts.title: Run it (about 15 min)
text: 1. MODEL: point to Bit's pile, say 'these are all mixed up'. Show the circle group — both ● circles together.
2. GUIDED: do the triangle group together — find each ▲ in the pile, draw it in the group box.
3. YOU TRY: children do the square group, then Exercise 3 on their own.
4. Connect: 'Computers sort too — that is how they keep things tidy and quick to find.'

parts.title: Answer key (modelled by the run-gate)
text: Pile ● ▲ ■ ● ▲ ■ → circle group = 2, triangle group = 2, square group = 2.
Ex 1 — 2 triangles. Ex 2 — 2 squares. Ex 3 (■ ● ■) — 2 squares (the circle is left out).

parts.title: Watch for & differentiate
text: Common slip: copying the whole pile into one group — remind them each group holds only one kind.
Simplify: sort with real objects by hand before drawing.
Extend: sort the same pile a different way (by size), or add a star ★ group.
Movement option: place shape cards on the floor and have children walk each to its group.

parts.title: Success looks like
parts.text: The child places every shape in the matching group and no group holds a different shape.
